q: what would happen if all insects disappeared
what would happen to the atmosphere if all insects disappeared
what if all insects went extinct
what would happen if insects were removed from the ecosystem
a: If all insects disappeared from Earth, the consequences would be catastrophic and rapid. Insects are essential pollinators for about 75% of flowering plants and 35% of global food crops. Without pollination, most fruits, vegetables, and nuts would disappear within a single growing season. Insects also form a critical part of the food chain: they are the primary food source for countless birds, reptiles, amphibians, fish, and small mammals. Without insects, these animals would starve, causing a cascading collapse of terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems. Insects are also essential decomposers, breaking down dead organic matter and recycling nutrients. Without them, dead plants and animals would accumulate, and soil fertility would decline dramatically. Regarding the atmosphere, insects play a relatively minor direct role in gas exchange compared to plants and microbes. However, the collapse of plant life due to lack of pollination would eventually reduce oxygen production and carbon dioxide absorption, though this would be a long-term effect. The most immediate impact would be agricultural: global food production would plummet, leading to widespread famine. Some estimates suggest that without insects, most terrestrial ecosystems would collapse within 50 years, and human civilization as we know it would be unsustainable.
